sourceHtml:
Every tool you give an agent sends its definition to the model on every request, and you pay for it as input tokens. A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server can add tens of thousands of tokens to the context window. The usual alternatives are a command-line tool (CLI) or a skill.

We measured it on one GitHub task with the GitHub MCP server, the gh CLI, and a gh skill, on Claude Haiku 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, GPT-6 Luna, and Gemini 3.8 Flash. On Sonnet 5.5, all three answered correctly, but the input tokens they used were very different. The CLI used 1,421, the skill used 3,315, and the MCP server used 59,417 with its default tools loaded. Here’s where the tokens go and how to cut them with our Tool Search server tool.

TL;DR

  • The GitHub MCP server’s 46 default tools add 19,436 tokens to every request on Claude Sonnet 5.5.

  • On Sonnet 5.5, one tool result, GitHub’s release object, cost about 20,400 tokens, more than all 46 definitions.

  • Tool Search cut the up-front cost of 46 tools to under 600 tokens. Over the whole task, it halved the cost on Sonnet 5.5 and raised it on Claude Haiku 5.5.

What is the difference between MCP, a CLI, and a skill?

All three give a model a capability. They differ in what the model reads before it can use it.

What the model sees up frontWhat it sees when it acts
MCP serverEvery tool’s name, description, and JSON schema, on every requestThe tool’s result, in whatever shape the server returns
CLIA shell tool and a line saying the CLI existsThe command’s output, which you shape with flags such as —json
SkillA one-line description of each skillThe skill’s SKILL.md file, once, then the command output

A CLI relies on the model already knowing the tool. A skill teaches the model how to use a tool, and the model loads the full instructions only when a task needs them.

How many tokens does an MCP server add to every request?

The reliable way to count them is to ask the model. Each provider writes tool definitions into the prompt in its own format before counting tokens, which a local tokenizer misses. Send the same request with and without the tools, and the difference in usage.prompt_tokens is what the tools cost on every turn.

Save this as mcp_cost.py. It speaks the 2025-06-18 version of MCP, which the GitHub server accepts.

"""How many prompt tokens does an MCP server add to every request? Ask the model."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

import requests

API = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}

def list_mcp_tools(command):
    """Start a stdio MCP server, run the handshake, and return its tools/list result."""
    proc = subprocess.Popen(command, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
                            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, text=True)

    def rpc(method, params, id=None):
        msg = {"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": method, "params": params}
        if id is not None:
            msg["id"] = id
        proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n")
        proc.stdin.flush()
        while id is not None:
            reply = json.loads(proc.stdout.readline())
            if reply.get("id") == id:
                return reply["result"]

    rpc("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-06-18", "capabilities": {},
                       "clientInfo": {"name": "mcp-cost", "version": "1"}}, id=1)
    rpc("notifications/initialized", {})
    tools, cursor, id = [], None, 2
    while True:  # follow nextCursor so servers that paginate tools/list are fully counted
        page = rpc("tools/list", {"cursor": cursor} if cursor else {}, id=id)
        tools += page["tools"]
        cursor, id = page.get("nextCursor"), id + 1
        if not cursor:
            break
    proc.kill()
    return tools

def prompt_tokens(model, tools=None):
    body = {"model": model, "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say ok."}]}
    if tools:
        body["tools"] = tools
    if model.startswith("google/"):
        # Google Vertex and Google AI Studio count the same tools differently, so pin one.
        body["provider"] = {"only": ["google-vertex"]}
    r = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, json=body, timeout=120)
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()["usage"]["prompt_tokens"]

if __name__ == "__main__":
    mcp_tools = list_mcp_tools(sys.argv[1:])
    # What an MCP client sends the model: each tool's name, description and input schema.
    tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": t["name"], "description": t.get("description", ""),
                                               "parameters": t["inputSchema"]}} for t in mcp_tools]
    print(f"{len(tools)} tools")
    for model in ["anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "openai/gpt-6-luna", "google/gemini-3.8-flash"]:
        added = prompt_tokens(model, tools) - prompt_tokens(model)
        print(f"{model:30} +{added:,} prompt tokens on every request")

Pass the server’s start command as arguments, as here for the GitHub MCP server v2.0.2.

$ python mcp_cost.py github-mcp-server stdio --toolsets=default
46 tools
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5     +19,436 prompt tokens on every request
openai/gpt-6-luna              +8,903 prompt tokens on every request
google/gemini-3.8-flash        +8,525 prompt tokens on every request

The cost grows with each tool you add. On Haiku 5.5, the issues toolset has 10 tools and adds 5,801 tokens. The users toolset has one tool and adds 619.

The model you use changes the count too. The same 46 tools cost 19,436 tokens on Haiku 5.5 but 8,903 on GPT-6 Luna, so measure on the model you plan to run.

Even the provider serving the model can change it. On Gemini 3.8 Flash, the 46 tools cost 8,525 tokens through Google Vertex and 13,010 through Google AI Studio. That’s why the script always sends Gemini requests to Google Vertex.

What does the same task cost with a CLI, a skill, and MCP?

We asked each model, “What is the latest release of the GitHub repository cli/cli, and what are the three most recently opened open issues in that repository with the label bug?” Each approach ran as a tool-calling loop on our Responses API, and we added up usage.input_tokens across requests.

  • CLI. One run_shell tool and the line “The GitHub CLI gh is installed and authenticated.”

  • Skill. The same tool, plus a one-line index pointing at a 1,492-character SKILL.md of gh recipes.

  • MCP. The server’s tools, scoped to the 2 the task needs, the default 46, or all 91.

We ran each combination three times on October 20, 2026, and show medians. Haiku 5.5 counts a prompt exactly as Sonnet 5.5 does, but it took extra turns in some runs, so we show Sonnet’s steadier tokens and billed cost.

ApproachSonnet 5.5 tokensSonnet 5.5 cost per taskGPT-6 Luna tokensGemini 3.8 Flash tokens
CLI1,421$0.00756275,292
Skill3,315$0.01181,5426,107
MCP, 2 tools23,228$0.055214,47917,267
MCP, 46 default tools59,417$0.1274116,28235,409
MCP, all 91 tools101,351$0.2113135,23853,289
MCP, 2 tools, results capped at 4,000 characters5,357$0.01912,7262,943

Every run in this table answered correctly. The failures came with Tool Search, covered below. On Sonnet 5.5, the default MCP server used 42 times the CLI’s input tokens and cost 17 times as much, $127 against $7.50 per 1,000 tasks. Output tokens cost five times as much as input on Sonnet 5.5, and the CLI run’s 463 output tokens were $0.0046 of its $0.0075.

The skill cost more than the bare CLI because the file stays in the conversation once the model reads it. For a CLI tool the model knows well, a skill is optional. For your own CLI, the skill is how the model learns the commands.

Why do MCP tool results cost as much as the definitions?

get_latest_release returned GitHub’s full release object, 42,182 characters, and 87% of it described the 22 download files. The model needed the tag and date, which is all gh release view returned.

$ gh release view -R cli/cli --json tagName,publishedAt
{"publishedAt":"2026-09-30T02:40:02Z","tagName":"v2.102.0"}

That object stays in the context window and is resent with every later request, and on Sonnet 5.5 it added about 20,400 tokens. Scoping the server to two tools cut the first request from 19,487 tokens to 1,406. The whole task still cost 23,228.

The table shows two fixes. First, expose only the tools the agent needs, with —tools=get_latest_release,list_issues or —toolsets=issues,repos. Second, shrink results in your client before the model sees them. A 4,000-character cap brought the scoped route to 5,357 tokens with every run correct, because GitHub puts the tag and date near the top.

The cap worked only because of where the fields happened to sit. Combined with Tool Search, the cap left Gemini 3.8 Flash and Haiku 5.5 with one correct answer in three runs each, and Gemini once hit our 12-request limit while retrying.

Keep whole fields instead, as —json does for the CLI. The GitHub server’s list_issues takes a fields argument, and asking for only number, title, and creation date cut its result from 8,336 characters to 714. Without it, the model decides the size. In four of six runs with 46 or 91 tools loaded, GPT-6 Luna asked for 100 issues with their full text and got 281,963 characters back.

Does Tool Search fix MCP’s context problem?

Tool Search removes most of the cost of tool definitions. You mark tools defer_loading: true and add {“type”: “openrouter:tool_search”}. We withhold the deferred definitions and send the search tool, plus any tools you left loaded. The model searches tool names and descriptions with a regular expression and calls a match on its next turn. It’s in beta and works with any model and provider on the Responses and Messages APIs.

With all 46 GitHub tools deferred, the cost before any search was 578 tokens on the Claude models, 144 on GPT-6 Luna, and 130 on Gemini 3.8 Flash.

This script sends one question with all 46 tools loaded, then deferred. Save it next to mcp_cost.py, since it reuses list_mcp_tools.

"""Send the same MCP tools with defer_loading and openrouter:tool_search, and compare prompt tokens."""
import os
import sys

import requests

from mcp_cost import list_mcp_tools

API = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}
QUESTION = "What is the latest release of the GitHub repository cli/cli?"

def ask(model, tools):
    r = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, timeout=300,
                      json={"model": model, "input": QUESTION, "tools": tools})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

mcp_tools = list_mcp_tools(sys.argv[1:])
# The Responses API takes function tools flat: type, name, description, parameters.
tools = [{"type": "function", "name": t["name"], "description": t.get("description", ""),
          "parameters": t["inputSchema"]} for t in mcp_tools]
deferred = [{"type": "openrouter:tool_search"}] + [{**t, "defer_loading": True} for t in tools]

for model in ["anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "openai/gpt-6-luna"]:
    for label, tool_list in [("all loaded", tools), ("tool search", deferred)]:
        res = ask(model, tool_list)
        steps = [f"search {o['query']!r}" if o["type"] == "openrouter:tool_search" else f"call {o['name']}"
                 for o in res["output"] if o["type"] in ("openrouter:tool_search", "function_call")]
        print(f"{model:28} {label:12} {res['usage']['input_tokens']:>6,} input tokens  {' -> '.join(steps)}")
$ python tool_search.py github-mcp-server stdio --toolsets=default
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5   all loaded   19,464 input tokens  call get_latest_release
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5   tool search   7,069 input tokens  search 'github|release' -> search 'latest release|list_releases|get_latest_release' -> call get_latest_release
openai/gpt-6-luna            all loaded    8,923 input tokens  call get_latest_release
openai/gpt-6-luna            tool search   4,453 input tokens  search 'github repository latest release cli cli' -> search 'github' -> search 'search web internet browser' -> search 'release' -> call get_latest_release

To try it on your agent, mark your MCP tools defer_loading: true, add {“type”: “openrouter:tool_search”}, and compare usage.input_tokens before and after.

The Tool Search rows vary with how the model searches. In five separate runs of this script, Haiku 5.5 used 2,134 to 13,225 tokens, rising with each search. GPT-6 Luna wrote phrases instead of patterns, made three to six searches, and once gave up without calling the tool. Our docs suggest keeping your three to five most-used tools loaded.

Over the whole task, the result depended on the model.

ModelMCP, 46 tools loadedTool Search, 46 deferredTool Search, 91 deferred
Claude Sonnet 5.559,41730,33431,615
GPT-6 Luna116,28225,54457,975
Gemini 3.8 Flash35,40937,56838,445
Claude Haiku 5.599,319154,62331,781

GPT-6 Luna’s loaded figure includes the 100-issue request described above.

On Sonnet 5.5, 91 deferred tools cost 1,281 tokens more than 46, where loading all 91 cost about 42,000 more. Tool Search doesn’t shrink tool results, and the release object still filled most of Sonnet’s second request.

Haiku 5.5 cost more with 46 deferred tools than with all loaded. In all three runs it asked list_issues for a field the tool doesn’t offer, then retried three or four times with arguments of the wrong type, such as labels as a string instead of an array. With all tools loaded, Haiku made the same mistake in two of three runs and fixed it on its next call. Cap the requests in your loop, and check tool errors when a run’s cost jumps.

Tool Search reveals tools by widening tool_choice, so a request that also forces a tool call fails.

400 `tool_choice` conflicts with `openrouter:tool_search`. Deferred tools are revealed through `tool_choice`, so it must be omitted or set to `{“type”: “allowed_tools”, …}`. Remove `tool_choice`, or drop `defer_loading` from your tools to use it as-is.

Chat Completions doesn’t accept openrouter:tool_search and returns a 400, so move that agent to the Responses or Messages API first.

MCP vs CLI vs skills: which should you use?

Use a CLI when one exists and your agent can run commands. When it can’t, use MCP, scoped and with small results.

Your situationUseFrom our runs on Sonnet 5.5
A well-known CLI exists and the agent can run commandsThe CLI1,421 tokens per task
Your own CLI, or one the model uses inconsistentlyThe CLI plus a skill3,315 tokens, same commands every run
No CLI, no shell, or you need the server’s auth and permissionsMCP, scoped to the tools you need23,228 tokens with 2 tools, against 59,417 with 46
A large tool library across many serversMCP with Tool SearchOn Sonnet 5.5, 91 deferred tools cost about what 46 did
Any MCP routeTrim tool results to the fields you need23,228 down to 5,357 tokens

If your agent has no shell, our Shell server tool gives any model a sandboxed one. In our Agent SDK, MCP Tools connects remote MCP servers, and the skills loader example adds a skill’s instructions only after the model asks for it.

We tested one server on one task, so run mcp_cost.py on yours before you decide.

Frequently asked questions

What is a CLI in an AI agent context?

A CLI (command-line interface) is a program you run with typed commands. An agent gets a shell tool and writes the commands itself. In our tests, the gh CLI used 1,421 input tokens on a GitHub task, against 59,417 for the GitHub MCP server.

What is the difference between an MCP server and a connector?

An MCP server exposes tools over the Model Context Protocol. A connector is what an app such as Claude calls its link to a remote MCP server. Our Agent SDK can connect remote MCP servers through MCP Tools.

Are skills replacing MCP?

No. A skill is instructions, usually for a CLI, that load only when a task needs them. MCP gives typed tools with their own auth and works without a shell. On OpenRouter, Tool Search lets you keep MCP and load each tool only when needed.

Does prompt caching fix MCP’s token cost?

It lowers the price of those tokens but doesn’t remove them. As of October 2026, on OpenRouter, cached input costs a tenth of the normal rate on Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna, per our live model prices, and still fills the context window.

How many MCP tools is too many?

Our Tool Search docs suggest deferring tools once definitions pass roughly 10,000 tokens or about 10 tools. The GitHub MCP server’s 46 default tools came to 19,436 tokens on Claude.

Next steps

  • Tool Search covers every option, including max_results.

  • Build a Reliable Tool-Calling Agent Loop shows the kind of loop our runs used, with an iteration cap.

  • OpenRouter Prompt Caching explains what cached tokens cost.

translation.html:
你为智能体提供的每个工具，都会在每次请求中将其定义发送给模型，而你需要为此支付输入 token 费用。一个 Model Context Protocol（模型上下文协议，MCP）服务器可能会向上下文窗口添加数万个 token。常见的替代方案是命令行工具（CLI）或技能。

我们用一项 GitHub 任务，对 GitHub MCP 服务器、gh CLI 和一项 gh 技能进行了测量，测试模型包括 Claude Haiku 5.5、Claude Sonnet 5.5、GPT-6 Luna 和 Gemini 3.8 Flash。在 Sonnet 5.5 上，三种方式都给出了正确答案，但使用的输入 token 数量差异很大。CLI 使用了 1,421 个，技能使用了 3,315 个，而加载默认工具的 MCP 服务器使用了 59,417 个。下面介绍这些 token 花在了哪里，以及如何用我们的 Tool Search 服务器工具减少消耗。

要点速览

  • GitHub MCP 服务器的 46 个默认工具，会在 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的每次请求中增加 19,436 个 token。

  • 在 Sonnet 5.5 上，单个工具结果，也就是 GitHub 的发布对象，就消耗了约 20,400 个 token，比全部 46 个工具定义加起来还多。

  • Tool Search 将 46 个工具的前期消耗降到了 600 个 token 以下。就整个任务而言，它将 Sonnet 5.5 的费用减半，却提高了 Claude Haiku 5.5 的费用。

MCP、CLI 和技能有什么区别？

三者都为模型提供某种能力。区别在于，模型在使用这项能力之前需要读取什么。

模型预先看到的内容模型执行操作时看到的内容
MCP 服务器每次请求中都包含每个工具的名称、描述和 JSON schema工具结果，其形式由服务器返回的内容决定
CLI一个 shell 工具，以及一句说明该 CLI 可用的话命令的输出，你可以用 —json 等标志控制其形式
技能每项技能的一行描述技能的 SKILL.md 文件，读取一次，之后是命令输出

CLI 依赖模型已经了解这个工具。技能则教模型如何使用工具，模型只会在任务需要时加载完整说明。

MCP 服务器会给每次请求增加多少 token？

可靠的计算方式是询问模型。各提供商都会先以自己的格式将工具定义写入提示词，再计算 token 数，本地分词器无法涵盖这一步。分别发送包含工具和不包含工具的相同请求，usage.prompt_tokens 的差值，就是这些工具在每一轮中的 token 开销。

将这段代码保存为 mcp_cost.py。它使用 MCP 的 2025-06-18 版本，GitHub 服务器支持该版本。

"""How many prompt tokens does an MCP server add to every request? Ask the model."""

import subprocess
import sys

import requests

                       "clientInfo": {"name": "mcp-cost", "version": "1"}}, id=1)

        tools += page["tools"]
        cursor, id = page.get("nextCursor"), id + 1
        if not cursor:

    return tools

def prompt_tokens(model, tools=None):
    body = {"model": model, "max_tokens": 16, "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Say ok."}]}
    if tools:

将服务器的启动命令作为参数传入，下面以 GitHub MCP 服务器 v2.0.2 为例。

$ python mcp_cost.py github-mcp-server stdio --toolsets=default
46 tools
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5     +19,436 prompt tokens on every request
openai/gpt-6-luna              +8,903 prompt tokens on every request
google/gemini-3.8-flash        +8,525 prompt tokens on every request

每增加一个工具，开销都会上升。在 Haiku 5.5 上，issues 工具集包含 10 个工具，会增加 5,801 个 token。users 工具集只有一个工具，会增加 619 个。

使用的模型也会影响计数。同样的 46 个工具在 Haiku 5.5 上消耗 19,436 个 token，在 GPT-6 Luna 上则消耗 8,903 个，因此应使用你计划运行的模型进行测量。

即便是提供模型服务的提供商，也可能改变计数。在 Gemini 3.8 Flash 上，这 46 个工具通过 Google Vertex 调用时消耗 8,525 个 token，通过 Google AI Studio 调用时则消耗 13,010 个。这就是脚本始终将 Gemini 请求发送到 Google Vertex 的原因。

用 CLI、技能和 MCP 完成同一任务，分别需要多少开销？

我们向每个模型提问：“GitHub 仓库 cli/cli 的最新发布版本是什么？该仓库中带有 bug 标签、仍处于打开状态且最近创建的三个 issue 是什么？”每种方式都在我们的 Responses API 上以工具调用循环运行，我们将各次请求的 usage.input_tokens 相加。

  • CLI。一个 run_shell 工具，加上一句“GitHub CLI gh 已安装并完成身份验证。”

  • 技能。使用同一个工具，另加一行索引，指向一份包含 gh 常用用法、长度为 1,492 个字符的 SKILL.md。

  • MCP。使用服务器提供的工具，范围分别限定为任务所需的 2 个工具、默认的 46 个工具，或全部 91 个工具。

我们在 2026 年 10 月 20 日将每种组合运行了三次，展示的是中位数。Haiku 5.5 对提示词的 token 计数方式与 Sonnet 5.5 完全相同，但在部分运行中多进行了几轮，因此我们展示 Sonnet 更稳定的 token 数和计费费用。

方式Sonnet 5.5 token 数Sonnet 5.5 每项任务费用GPT-6 Luna token 数Gemini 3.8 Flash token 数
CLI1,421$0.00756275,292
技能3,315$0.01181,5426,107
MCP，2 个工具23,228$0.055214,47917,267
MCP，46 个默认工具59,417$0.1274116,28235,409
MCP，全部 91 个工具101,351$0.2113135,23853,289
MCP，2 个工具，结果限制为 4,000 个字符5,357$0.01912,7262,943

此表中的每次运行都给出了正确答案。失败发生在使用 Tool Search 时，下文会介绍。在 Sonnet 5.5 上，默认 MCP 服务器使用的输入 token 是 CLI 的 42 倍，费用是其 17 倍，每 1,000 项任务分别为 127 美元和 7.50 美元。Sonnet 5.5 的输出 token 单价是输入的五倍，CLI 运行中的 463 个输出 token 产生了 0.0046 美元费用，占其总费用 0.0075 美元的一部分。

技能比单独使用 CLI 的开销更高，因为模型读取文件后，文件内容会一直留在对话中。对于模型熟悉的 CLI 工具，技能是可选的。对于你自己的 CLI，技能则是模型学习命令的途径。

为什么 MCP 工具结果的开销能与工具定义一样高？

get_latest_release 返回了 GitHub 的完整发布对象，共 42,182 个字符，其中 87% 都在描述 22 个下载文件。模型需要的是标签和日期，而 gh release view 只返回了这些信息。

$ gh release view -R cli/cli --json tagName,publishedAt
{"publishedAt":"2026-09-30T02:40:02Z","tagName":"v2.102.0"}

该对象会留在上下文窗口中，并随之后的每次请求重新发送，在 Sonnet 5.5 上增加了约 20,400 个 token。将服务器的范围限定为两个工具后，首次请求从 19,487 个 token 降到了 1,406 个。整个任务仍消耗了 23,228 个。

表格展示了两种解决办法。第一，只暴露智能体需要的工具，使用 —tools=get_latest_release,list_issues 或 —toolsets=issues,repos。第二，在模型看到结果之前，先在客户端缩减结果。将结果限制为 4,000 个字符后，限定工具范围的方案降到了 5,357 个 token，而且每次运行都回答正确，因为 GitHub 将标签和日期放在靠近开头的位置。

这一限制之所以有效，只是因为字段恰好位于那些位置。与 Tool Search 结合后，Gemini 3.8 Flash 和 Haiku 5.5 各自的三次运行中都只有一次回答正确，而且 Gemini 有一次在重试时触及了我们设定的 12 次请求上限。

应改为保留完整字段，就像 CLI 的 —json 所做的那样。GitHub 服务器的 list_issues 接受 fields 参数，只请求编号、标题和创建日期，就将结果从 8,336 个字符缩减到了 714 个。不指定该参数时，结果大小由模型决定。在加载 46 个或 91 个工具的六次运行中，GPT-6 Luna 有四次请求了 100 个 issue 及其完整正文，收到了 281,963 个字符。

Tool Search 能解决 MCP 的上下文问题吗？

Tool Search 消除了工具定义的大部分开销。你将工具标记为 defer_loading: true，并添加 {“type”: “openrouter:tool_search”}。我们会暂不发送延迟加载的定义，只发送搜索工具，以及你保留为已加载状态的工具。模型用正则表达式搜索工具名称和描述，并在下一轮调用匹配的工具。该功能处于测试阶段，可在 Responses 和 Messages API 上配合任何模型和提供商使用。

将全部 46 个 GitHub 工具设为延迟加载后，在任何搜索发生之前，Claude 模型的开销为 578 个 token，GPT-6 Luna 为 144 个，Gemini 3.8 Flash 为 130 个。

这个脚本会针对同一个问题，先在加载全部 46 个工具的情况下发送一次，再在延迟加载的情况下发送一次。请将它保存在 mcp_cost.py 旁边，因为它会复用 list_mcp_tools。

"""Send the same MCP tools with defer_loading and openrouter:tool_search, and compare prompt tokens."""
import os
import sys

import requests

from mcp_cost import list_mcp_tools

API = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses"
HEADERS = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['OPENROUTER_API_KEY']}"}
QUESTION = "What is the latest release of the GitHub repository cli/cli?"

def ask(model, tools):
    r = requests.post(API, headers=HEADERS, timeout=300,
                      json={"model": model, "input": QUESTION, "tools": tools})
    r.raise_for_status()
    return r.json()

mcp_tools = list_mcp_tools(sys.argv[1:])
# The Responses API takes function tools flat: type, name, description, parameters.
tools = [{"type": "function", "name": t["name"], "description": t.get("description", ""),
          "parameters": t["inputSchema"]} for t in mcp_tools]
deferred = [{"type": "openrouter:tool_search"}] + [{**t, "defer_loading": True} for t in tools]

for model in ["anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5", "openai/gpt-6-luna"]:
    for label, tool_list in [("all loaded", tools), ("tool search", deferred)]:
        res = ask(model, tool_list)
        steps = [f"search {o['query']!r}" if o["type"] == "openrouter:tool_search" else f"call {o['name']}"
                 for o in res["output"] if o["type"] in ("openrouter:tool_search", "function_call")]
        print(f"{model:28} {label:12} {res['usage']['input_tokens']:>6,} input tokens  {' -> '.join(steps)}")
$ python tool_search.py github-mcp-server stdio --toolsets=default
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5   all loaded   19,464 input tokens  call get_latest_release
anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5   tool search   7,069 input tokens  search 'github|release' -> search 'latest release|list_releases|get_latest_release' -> call get_latest_release
openai/gpt-6-luna            all loaded    8,923 input tokens  call get_latest_release
openai/gpt-6-luna            tool search   4,453 input tokens  search 'github repository latest release cli cli' -> search 'github' -> search 'search web internet browser' -> search 'release' -> call get_latest_release

要在你的智能体上试用，请将 MCP 工具标记为 defer_loading: true，添加 {“type”: “openrouter:tool_search”}，并比较前后的 usage.input_tokens。

Tool Search 各行的数据会随模型的搜索方式变化。在单独运行该脚本的五次测试中，Haiku 5.5 使用了 2,134 至 13,225 个 token，消耗随着每次搜索增加。GPT-6 Luna 写的是短语而非匹配模式，进行了三到六次搜索，有一次在未调用工具的情况下就放弃了。我们的文档建议，让最常用的三到五个工具保持加载状态。

GPT-6 Luna 在工具已加载情况下的数据，包含了上文所述的 100 个 issue 请求。

在 Sonnet 5.5 上，延迟加载 91 个工具比延迟加载 46 个多消耗 1,281 个 token，而直接加载全部 91 个工具则多消耗约 42,000 个。Tool Search 不会缩减工具结果，发布对象仍占据了 Sonnet 第二次请求的大部分内容。

Haiku 5.5 延迟加载 46 个工具时的费用，比全部加载时更高。三次运行中，它都向 list_issues 请求了该工具不提供的字段，随后又使用错误类型的参数重试了三到四次，例如将 labels 作为字符串而非数组传入。全部工具都加载时，Haiku 在三次运行中有两次犯了同样的错误，并在下一次调用中修正。请为循环设置请求次数上限，并在某次运行费用激增时检查工具错误。

Tool Search 通过扩大 tool_choice 的可选范围来提供工具，因此同时强制调用工具的请求会失败。

400：`tool_choice` 与 `openrouter:tool_search` 冲突。延迟加载的工具通过 `tool_choice` 提供，因此必须省略该参数，或将其设置为 `{“type”: “allowed_tools”, …}`。请移除 `tool_choice`，或从工具中移除 `defer_loading`，以按原样使用它。

Chat Completions 不接受 openrouter:tool_search，会返回 400，因此请先将该智能体迁移到 Responses 或 Messages API。

MCP、CLI 和技能：应该用哪一种？

如果已有 CLI，而且你的智能体可以运行命令，就使用 CLI。如果无法运行命令，就使用 MCP，限定工具范围并缩小结果。

如果你的智能体没有 shell，我们的 Shell 服务器工具可以为任何模型提供一个沙盒化的 shell。在我们的 Agent SDK 中，MCP Tools 用于连接远程 MCP 服务器，而技能加载器示例只会在模型提出请求后，才添加技能的说明。

我们只在一个服务器上测试了一项任务，因此请先针对你的服务器运行 mcp_cost.py，再做决定。

常见问题

在 AI 智能体场景中，CLI 是什么？

CLI（命令行界面）是通过键入命令运行的程序。智能体获得一个 shell 工具后，会自行编写命令。在我们的测试中，gh CLI 完成一项 GitHub 任务使用了 1,421 个输入 token，而 GitHub MCP 服务器使用了 59,417 个。

MCP 服务器与连接器有什么区别？

MCP 服务器通过 Model Context Protocol 提供工具。连接器则是 Claude 等应用对其与远程 MCP 服务器之间连接的称呼。我们的 Agent SDK 可以通过 MCP Tools 连接远程 MCP 服务器。

技能正在取代 MCP 吗？

没有。技能是一组说明，通常用于 CLI，只有任务需要时才会加载。MCP 提供带有类型定义和自身身份验证机制的工具，无需 shell 也能使用。在 OpenRouter 上，Tool Search 让你可以继续使用 MCP，并仅在需要时加载各个工具。

提示词缓存能解决 MCP 的 token 费用问题吗？

它会降低这些 token 的价格，但不会消除它们。截至 2026 年 10 月，根据我们的实时模型价格，在 OpenRouter 上，Claude Haiku 5.5 和 GPT-6 Luna 的缓存输入价格为正常费率的十分之一，但仍会占用上下文窗口。

MCP 工具多到什么程度算太多？

我们的 Tool Search 文档建议，当工具定义超过约 10,000 个 token，或工具数量达到约 10 个时，就采用延迟加载。GitHub MCP 服务器的 46 个默认工具在 Claude 上合计为 19,436 个 token。
